objections.claim: The spec's load-bearing structural defense — call 2 adjudicates against a reconstruction the arguments could not colour — rests entirely on the faithfulness of a free-prose model synthesis that is validated only for non-emptiness. A boilerplate or hallucinated reconstruction passes the per-section gate and grounds a wrong adjudication, so the defense collapses to exactly the prompt-compliance reliance the two-call split was built to replace.
objections.evidence: The spec's reconstruction-validation decision ("per-section non-empty, not shape-only") admits "it cannot judge substance *quality* — that residual is exactly what the born-verifiable discrimination smoke guards." But the smoke (DONE: "the defect case is not ruled AFFIRM_SPEC and the taste case is not ruled UPHOLD_REVIEW") tests the *ruling*, never the reconstruction. A model asked to "reconstruct requirements and existing behaviour" will almost always emit non-empty prose, so the gate nearly always passes, and the defense's strength is the model's faithfulness — the same unverifiable property the spec rejected in the one-call form ("the defence is only as strong as the model's compliance").
objections.predicted_consequence: A judge that produces plausible-but-ungrounded reconstructions (or a spec injection that steers the reconstruction through prose not on the directive scrub list) passes every gate and grounds call 2 against a fabricated picture — the injection surface the two-call split exists to close is reopened, and no deterministic check in the shipped design detects it.

objections.claim: The spec-review-outage disposition gives the reviewer an in-turn retry loop (`prep.spec_review_outage_retry_limit`, default 2), but the judge dispatch has none: a transport outage marks the proposition `resolution: parked`. With N propositions × 2 calls, a single transient outage in any call parks a blocking proposition and fails the entire would-be-park pass to needs-human — at L4, one transient blip in a 10-call sequence escalates to a human.
objections.evidence: The spec's admit roll-up: "a judge-dispatch failure (reconstruction empty/failed, transport outage, non-conformant ruling) marks the proposition resolution: parked" and "a parked blocking proposition ... forces admit:false → needs-human." The reviewer's outage disposition (spec-review-outage section) explicitly retries in-turn; the judge dispatch section contains no retry. The judge is strictly more outage-sensitive (2N calls vs one reviewer call) yet strictly less resilient.
objections.predicted_consequence: At L4, a transient backend blip in any of the 2N judge calls converts a would-be-park resolution into a human escalation, so the terminal judge pass fails to a human on noise — the exact operational fragility the reviewer's retry loop was added to avoid, now multiplied by 2N.

objections.claim: The orchestrator — the party that benefits from admission — applies the correction, and the only check is literal-presence plus whole-file hash change. The orchestrator can add the verification literal anywhere (a comment, an unrelated section) and trivially change the hash, resolving an UPHOLD_REVIEW proposition with a non-fix. The spec's deferral to the build-stage review does not close this: that review re-runs the repo's UNIT rung, which will not catch an architectural defect the judge's correction was supposed to fix.
objections.evidence: The spec's correction-applied decision: "the check requires the correction.verification literal to appear in the corrected spec and the whole-spec-file hash to differ ... it is deliberately a change-detection + literal-presence proxy, not proof the defect is fixed." The DONE criterion is worded to match: "the verification literal is present in the changed spec file." The build-stage bound is "the build-stage review/holdout that re-reads the changed spec" — which, per the post-merge-verification contract, re-runs the UNIT rung.
objections.predicted_consequence: An UPHOLD_REVIEW proposition resolves with a correction that adds the literal without addressing the defect, the spec is admitted, and the defect survives to the build stage where the UNIT-rung re-check does not exercise it — the one step where the untrusted party has full control is the one step whose check is a paste-and-change proxy.

objections.claim: The gate's stated security property is "a bare caller flag can never assert final human-free authority" (the `l4_unratified` coercion). Its corroboration source is the run-ledger `level` at `$FAFF_RUN_DIR`, which the spec says is "stamped once at run start by the operator's `faff lights-out` invocation … and is immutable for the run's life — the orchestrator does not write or raise it mid-run." But the spec establishes no mechanism for that immutability — no refusal-to-overwrite in `faff lights-out`, no digest/signature, no out-of-band operator artifact. The orchestrator is the same actor that shells `faff` for every other step and is the admission-benefiting party the spec's own threat model names. If the orchestrator can write or re-mint `run-ledger.json` (or run `faff lights-out` mid-run), it self-authorizes L4 and the gate passes. The spec's L4-authority decision concedes the run-ledger level "is not one of [the] deterministic guards that a within-run orchestrator cannot satisfy by fiat," yet the same decision claims pinning to the "immutable launch stamp" "removes the specific 'orchestrator forges its own L4 authority' reading" — those two statements only reconcile if the ledger is genuinely untamperable, which the spec asserts rather than proves.
objections.evidence: §7 "L4 authority derives from the operator's run launch, not an orchestrator mid-run write" ("stamped once at run start … immutable for the run's life … the orchestrator does not write or raise it mid-run"); §4 `AdmitResult.level` ("a caller-asserted L4 with no run-ledger corroboration is coerced down to L3"); §7 L4-ratification gate ("a bare `--level L4` with no run-ledger `L4` is coerced to effective L3 … so a caller flag alone can never assert final human-free authority"); §7 L4-authority decision ("the run-ledger level is not one of them [the guards an orchestrator cannot satisfy by fiat] … this decision removes only the specific 'orchestrator forges its own L4 authority' reading by pinning the level to the immutable launch stamp").
objections.predicted_consequence: An orchestrator that edits or re-mints the run-ledger `level` to `L4` passes the `l4_unratified` gate and reaches a final human-free ADMIT, so the gate stops a caller flag but not the admission-benefiting actor it exists to constrain — the "final human-free authority" boundary is forgeable by the very party the gate is meant to bind.

objections.claim: The `infosec_major` floor is computed "over the ledger's retained `{lens, severity}`" (the standing residue the judge adjudicated), but the v1 `infosec_major_free_latest` input the roll-up consumes is derived from the *latest in-window round's* standing objections (`spec-judge-evidence.js` `infosecMajorFree(standingObjections)`). The judge's `UPHOLD_REVIEW`/`SYNTHESIZE` corrections are applied to the *spec*, not to the round record, so the round's objection list is unchanged after a correction. If the residue's infosec-major objection is one the judge ruled `AFFIRM_SPEC` (reviewer failed to establish a material defect) and the orchestrator's correction does not remove it from the round record, the floor still vetoes — that is the safe direction. The gap is the reverse: the floor is a *round-derived* signal, but the roll-up's other inputs (rulings, corrections, `pre_ruling_spec_sha`) are *judge-pass-derived*. The two sources can disagree about which objections are "standing" after the judge pass, and the spec never states which is authoritative for the floor. If the floor is meant to be "no standing major-or-worse infosec objection *after the judge pass*," it should be computed from the resolved ledger, not the pre-judge round.
objections.evidence: §4 `AdmitResult.floor_veto` ("subset of {…\"infosec_major\"…}"); §6 holdout ("The admit roll-up emits `admit: false` and `floor_veto` includes `\"infosec_major\"` whenever `infosec_major_free` over the retained lens tag is false, regardless of every per-proposition outcome"); §5 admit roll-up ("`floor_pass := blocker_free_latest ∧ infosec_major_free ∧ l4_gates`"); `spec-judge-evidence.js` `infosecMajorFree(standingObjections)` (derived from the latest round's `objections`, not the ledger).
objections.predicted_consequence: The infosec floor and the per-proposition rulings can be computed over different objection sets (round-derived vs. ledger-derived), so a judge pass that resolves an infosec-major proposition by correction still sees the floor veto (safe) — but the spec's claim that the floor is "over the retained lens tag" (ledger) and the v1 implementation's "over the latest round" (round) are not reconciled, leaving the floor's input source ambiguous and the floor potentially computed over a stale or mismatched objection set.

objections.claim: The DONE item "The judge system prompts run Phase 1 (reconstruct, blind to positions) in call 1 and Phase 2 (adjudicate A/B) in call 2, and mark the spec/case file/governing block as untrusted data" is a prompt-content assertion with no pass/fail line. The spec defines no test, scenario, or fixture that inspects the prompt text, and the two-call *structural* defence (the architectural-major decision) is explicitly the load-bearing control — so a build that ships a Phase-1 prompt that does not actually instruct reconstruction (or a Phase-2 prompt that does not mark the inputs untrusted) satisfies every named AC while the injection defence silently degrades to "whatever the model happens to do."
objections.evidence: DONE item under "From HOW (judge dispatch, faff-prep)" (the system-prompts bullet); the "Structural two-call injection defence" and "L4 injection-admit residual risk" decisions both rest on the prompts doing their job.
objections.predicted_consequence: done cannot be decided for that DONE item — there is no observation that distinguishes a correct Phase-1/Phase-2 prompt from a wrong one, so the single most security-relevant prompt in the ticket is unverifiable as written. A minimal fix is a prompt-content assertion (e.g. the Phase-1 prompt must contain the four named reconstruction section keys and must not contain the argument field names; the Phase-2 prompt must contain the untrusted-data framing), which makes the item decidable.

objections.claim: The in-ticket discrimination run (the one born-verifiable guard against a constant-ruling judge) says a transport outage "retries (bounded)" and that only an all-retries-exhausted outage records a skip that blocks. But the spec never states the retry bound (count, backoff, or deadline), so the boundary between "transient outage → retry clears → green" and "exhausted outage → skip → needs-human block" is not pinned. A build could pick any bound (or effectively none) and still satisfy the wording.
objections.evidence: DONE item "In-ticket discrimination run (not deferred)" and the "In-ticket discrimination smoke: an outage retries, and an exhausted outage blocks rather than passes" decision; the scenario "Given the committed discriminating case pair ... a transport outage retries (bounded) and an all-retries-exhausted outage BLOCKS the engineering gate."
objections.predicted_consequence: the retry/exhaustion boundary of the ticket's only behavioural guard is not decidable — a reviewer cannot tell whether a given build's retry policy matches the spec, and the "never passes green on outage" property is only as strong as an unspecified bound. Naming the bound (e.g. N attempts within the adversarial deadline) makes it checkable.
